title: Dicky Wells, 'Fat Fanny' and the Basie band as a happy family
summary: Dicky Wells greeted her in the band, and Earle Warren and others called her 'Fat Fanny'. She describes the band as a big happy family with Basie as the nicest boss, who never used authority.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Listen, when you went with that Band it must have been funny to find old Dicky Wells up there. You were both at the same school.
What did Dicky have to say?
"Hey Homey". Earle Warren and them, Well, /they used to call me Fanny. They used to call me Fat Fanny, because I had a little bitty waist line, you know, and kind of big hips and legs.
Yeah. And I said, now look here, don't be calling me that but they kept on calling me that. That's what they all used to call me.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
I don't think there was a band that has as much fun as a band as that band did, do you?
No. It was such a nice group. Just like a big happy family.
And I mean they were so eager to get to work every night, weren't they?
I mean, that's the biggest thing with a band when it's making history. Very exciting, isn't it. And the guys, I mean, they're fond of Basie, aren't they?
Oh yes, yes indeed. He was the nicest boss. He really was. He was just one of the band members.
And he never tried to use authority or nothing, you know. Never. He was just always very nice and they'd all sit down and talk and have drinks together. It was just a big happy family.
Yeah. He didn't get mad at anybody if they got drunk on the job?
No, well he didn't want that.
